+# Targeted async and synchronization validation
+
+Required when the reviewed change affects lock acquisition/progress, cancellation,
+queue/permit ownership, task termination or a shared-state synchronization protocol.
+Determine scope from affected callers and invariants, not just new async/atomic tokens.
+Routine async syntax or unchanged runtime internals do not themselves require a Loom
+model. Assess async execution and custom synchronization separately in the report.
+
+## Async behavior: exercise the transitions
+
+Map the affected paths to locks held, await points, ownership of queued items/permits,
+spawned tasks, and externally visible effects. Establish the contract before testing:
+what must complete, what cancellation may discard, and what must have stopped on return.
+
+For applicable behaviors require named targeted tests:
+
+- **Deadlocks/progress:** exercise nested/reentrant acquisition, competing lock order
+  and callbacks while guards are live. Use channels/barriers or controlled polling to
+  reach the contested state. Bound the test and the process. An executor timer cannot
+  rescue a thread blocked by a synchronous lock: use an external watchdog for that case.
+  A slow or killed test alone does not prove deadlock. Show the reached state and wait
+  cycle; distinguish setup/time-limit failures from a demonstrated progress violation.
+- **Cancellation:** suspend at relevant await/select boundaries before and after state
+  mutation; drop/abort the future and inspect queue contents, permits, resources and
+  partial effects. Exercise channel closure and partial I/O where the contract requires
+  it. Happy-path completion is not cancellation evidence. Do not rely on arbitrary sleeps
+  to make the cancellation window occur; explicit polling/handshakes are preferable.
+- **Task lifecycle:** distinguish dropping a handle, requesting abort and observing
+  termination. Verify the absence of prohibited effects after stop/shutdown returns,
+  including destructor completion when required. Use a worker held at a known boundary
+  and a controlled subsequent signal/effect. Account for running spawn_blocking jobs
+  and cooperative shutdown: abort alone is not a completion barrier.
+
+Run on the runtime/configuration relevant to the contract. State current-thread vs
+multi-thread, clock configuration, scheduling controls, deadlines, commands, test
+names/counts, logs and source hashes. Test only applicable behaviors; N/A needs a reason.
+Missing or unrelated tests are NOT RUN, never PASS for these checks.
+
+## Synchronization: require Loom and a separate argument
+
+For a changed custom shared-state synchronization protocol (atomic publication,
+lock-free algorithms, or inter-thread lock/notification protocols), require a targeted
+Loom model and an independent ordering/invariant argument. Tokio task scheduling and
+cancellation tests above do not substitute for Loom; Loom does not model all Tokio or
+OS behavior either. Pure task lifecycle code without a custom inter-thread protocol
+may mark sync-scope NONE, while still requiring async tests.
+
+Prefer the exact reviewed implementation with cfg-selected Loom primitives. Confirm
+that the exercised types really are Loom's tracked atomics/locks/Arc/thread; a model
+that still uses std atomics for the relevant state cannot validate the protocol.
+When direct instrumentation is unavailable, an isolated adaptation may substitute only
+concurrency primitives and scheduling hooks. Preserve operations, ordering modes,
+control flow and assertions; record the diff/mapping and source hashes. A separately
+rewritten similar algorithm is not evidence. If the mapping cannot preserve the relevant
+behavior, report the gap and ESCALATE rather than weakening the claim or the model.
+
+Model meaningful competing actions and assert the actual contract, not merely that
+threads finish. Include relevant publication/read, notification/wakeup, failed CAS,
+reuse or reclamation paths as applicable. Respect documented caller preconditions;
+do not invent multiple writers when the contract is explicitly one-shot/single-writer.
+A passing model must be non-vacuous: identify operations/interleavings it explores.
+
+Record Loom and dependency versions, cfg/features, thread/operation counts, preemption
+bounds, branch/permutation/time limits, completion and logs. A bounded completed model
+supports only its stated bounds and assumptions; it is not a proof of all executions.
+A truncated, timed-out, unsupported or zero-test model is NOT RUN for approval. Provide
+a synchronization argument identifying the invariant, atomic modification/orderings,
+release/acquire or lock handoff, linearization/progress obligations where relevant.
+Do not report Relaxed as inherently wrong: independent telemetry may need atomicity
+only. A model counterexample must obey the real API contract and correspond to source.
+
+## Isolated probes, verdicts and limits
+
+Use existing adequate tests/models first. When execution is authorized and coverage
+is absent, create bounded probes outside the reviewed repository using exact source
+copies/imports. Do not repair the implementation or alter Git/source/configuration.
+Record harness changes and verify source hashes. Do not install tools or dependencies
+outside session authorization. Use exact-version dependency contracts when needed.
+
+Missing applicable async evidence, unavailable/incomplete Loom or an unresolved
+synchronization argument requires ESCALATE, not APPROVE or a fabricated P1. A verified
+counterexample is FAIL and supports REQUEST_CHANGES. If both proved blockers and
+unresolved risks remain, use ESCALATE and list the proved defects too. NONE/N/A needs
+a scope-based explanation. Existing memory-validation obligations still apply whenever
+the concurrent code changes unsafe/FFI invariants; Loom does not replace Miri.
+
+Proposed concurrency fixes remain candidates until tested. Where practical, use a
+known-good control or check that the regression fails before and passes after a fix,
+without changing the reviewed tree. Do not count an invalid harness or resource timeout
+as successful defect detection. Report scope limitations explicitly.
+
+References: [Loom](https://docs.rs/loom/),
+[Tokio task cancellation](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/task/index.html#cancellation),
+[atomic ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/atomic/enum.Ordering.html).

+# Targeted memory validation
+
+Required for changed unsafe/FFI code and safe callers that change its lifetime,
+ownership, aliasing or synchronization assumptions. A grep for new `unsafe` tokens
+alone is not sufficient to determine scope. A safe-only change with no affected
+unsafe invariant may report memory-scope NONE with a reason.
+
+## Establish the invariant and exercise it
+
+For each affected memory boundary, record the owner, allocation/free pairing,
+origin and validity of retained pointers, allowed reads/writes, lifetime, alignment,
+and thread/reentrancy obligations. Read the implementation and actual callers.
+
+Check aliasing separately from liveness: a stable address and a live allocation do
+not establish that an earlier pointer remains usable. Trace owner moves, reference
+creation and reborrowing, mutable/exclusive access, callbacks and destruction. Include
+Box/Vec ownership transitions, raw-pointer conversions, pinning assumptions and any
+manual Send/Sync proof. A SAFETY comment is a claim to verify, not evidence by itself.
+
+Map each relevant invariant to a named targeted test. For retained FFI pointers,
+exercise access after the constructor returns and the owner moves, while the owner
+is alive, during deregistration when the contract permits it, and until callback
+quiescence. Check bounds/alignment and exceptional paths where applicable. Tests must
+respect the unsafe API caller's documented obligations; violations by an invalid
+mock do not prove a defect in the wrapper.
+
+Run these tests under Miri on the reviewed source. Zero tests or unrelated tests
+are NOT RUN for this memory gate, even if cargo exits successfully. Record the test
+names, exercised paths, count, exact command, toolchain/commit, MIRIFLAGS, result and
+log path. A targeted PASS is necessary for approval, but is not a soundness proof.
+
+If adequate tests are absent and execution is authorized, build bounded probes in
+an isolated temporary workspace. Copy/import the exact reviewed implementation,
+record source hashes and dependencies/configuration, and write only the harness
+there. Do not repair or simplify the implementation to make it testable. Do not edit
+the reviewed repository. If this requires unavailable permissions or cannot preserve
+the relevant behavior, report the gap and ESCALATE rather than declare safety.
+
+For Miri setup, check available toolchains/components and existing sysroot first.
+Miri may install rust-src during first-use setup; follow session permissions and do
+not let a supposedly read-only check silently install components when prohibited.
+Use a timeout. Run suspected UB only in Miri or an authorized diagnostic environment,
+never as an ordinary native reproducer.
+
+## FFI evidence boundaries
+
+Miri cannot validate arbitrary native foreign libraries. A Rust callback or shim can
+exercise the wrapper's pointer/lifetime behavior only when it obeys the documented
+ABI and contract. State this limit. Missing provider guarantees (retention,
+quiescence, allocator ownership, thread affinity, unwinding) remain unresolved even
+if a guessed shim passes. Request the versioned SDK contract or implementation audit
+needed to close the question; do not invent a vendor defect.
+
+## Failures and conflicting models
+
+Keep the original failing log. Distinguish demonstrated invalid accesses (for example
+freed allocation or out-of-bounds) from experimental alias-model diagnostics. For an
+aliasing diagnostic, inspect the creation/invalidation/access chain and, where useful
+and supported, compare Stacked Borrows with Tree Borrows on the same source and test.
+Record both configurations. Do not turn off checks to obtain a passing result, and do
+not choose whichever model passes as proof. Disagreement means aliasing UNRESOLVED
+and verdict ESCALATE pending a justified provenance argument or a validated redesign.
+
+For any proposed unsafe/FFI fix, re-check both ownership and aliasing. Keeping an
+allocation alive is not enough. An untested suggested fix must be labeled a candidate;
+do not claim that it closes the safety issue. Test authorized fixes in a separate copy
+and keep original and modified evidence distinct.
+
+## Report and verdict
+
+Fill `## Memory safety` for every review. NONE means no affected memory boundary;
+REQUIRED needs targeted Miri evidence and an aliasing argument. Missing tests,
+unsupported operations, unknown external guarantees or conflicting models mean
+UNRESOLVED and ESCALATE. A clearly demonstrated violation may use FAIL and
+REQUEST_CHANGES. If both a proved defect and unresolved risks exist, use ESCALATE and
+list the proved blockers too. Never convert missing evidence into a fabricated P1.
+
+References: [Miri](https://github.com/rust-lang/miri) and
+[unsafe-code guidelines](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines).

+# Optional local reviewdog
+
+Run from the reviewed Cargo workspace:
+
+```bash
+RUST_REVIEWDOG=1 bash .agents/skills/rust-pr-review/scripts/gates.sh
+```
+
+The helper runs Clippy once, preserves raw uncolored short diagnostics and its exit
+code in a printed temporary evidence directory, then feeds that file to reviewdog.
+It uses the local reporter only and installs nothing. Missing reviewdog falls back
+to the raw diagnostics. Its errors/status are separate from the Clippy gate.
+`RUST_REVIEWDOG_BIN` can select an existing executable by name or absolute path.
+Retain the evidence files until the review is complete.
+
+Default filtering is `nofilter`. For tracked branch plus working-tree changes, set
+`RUST_REVIEWDOG_BASE` to the already resolved review base SHA. For working-tree-only
+review, use HEAD. For a committed-only scope, use matching checkout/CI evidence;
+this helper's diff includes local edits. Invalid bases fall back to unfiltered output.
+Git diff excludes untracked files: omit the base when they are in scope.
+
+Always derive the `clippy` gate from Clippy's exit status, not reviewdog's report or
+exit status. Inspect raw output on compilation failure, parser failure or an empty
+report. A successful reviewdog process with zero displayed diagnostics is not a
+passing lint check. Record presentation failures/omissions separately in the report;
+reviewdog does not replace Miri, Loom, tests or semantic review.
+
+If the project already has `.reviewdog.yml` or `.reviewdog.yaml`, prefer its relevant
+lint runners with `-reporter=local -filter-mode=nofilter -fail-level=warning` for
+project presentation. Still run the Clippy gate independently: config runners may
+filter, mask failures or use different flags. Do not automatically execute every
+runner. Do not feed RTK-condensed output to a parser; use `rtk bypass` for a producer
+if it is intercepted. The helper calls Cargo directly without a condensing wrapper.
+Remote reporters require an explicit request to publish results.

+# Verify rust-analyzer through rust-lsp
+
+At the start of Rust review, discover the `rust-lsp` skill and read its instructions
+if available. Discover the current Rust LSP tool APIs; do not invent tool names or
+assume that `rust-analyzer --version`, a skill listing or a plugin registration
+proves that the integration can analyze this project.
+
+Use a read-only workspace probe exposed by the integration (for example
+`analyzer_status` with the absolute `workspace_root`, if available). Check its
+payload as well as its error status: a response describing failed workspace loading
+is not success. If no status API exists, use a read-only semantic query on a known
+symbol in an in-scope Rust file. Allow bounded initialization using the integration's
+documented behavior; do not retry indefinitely. Record failures, timeouts, partial
+indexing, unsupported features and unresolved macros.
+
+If the skill or APIs are missing, follow the rust-lsp setup instructions only within
+existing authorization. Review alone does not authorize installation: its setup may
+install a rustup component and a Cargo package from Git. If setup is unauthorized,
+fails or still exposes no usable APIs, record UNAVAILABLE and continue source review.
+Do not change global configuration or install packages merely to turn this status green.
+
+When available, use semantic queries for the reviewed symbols: definitions,
+references, hover/types or implementations, according to the exposed APIs. Read the
+resolved source. Do not rename symbols or apply workspace edits during review.
+An empty result, tool discovery or a health probe alone does not establish actual
+semantic use. Count use only after a successful relevant query with interpretable
+results; record its target and what it established.
+
+## Report
+
+Always include `## Tooling` in a standalone report:
+
+- `rust-lsp: AVAILABLE` means a workspace probe or semantic query confirmed usable
+  analysis for the reviewed scope. Otherwise use `UNAVAILABLE` with the reason.
+- `lsp-used: YES` means at least one relevant semantic query succeeded. A successful
+  health check alone means `NO`. If the integration later fails, describe its partial
+  coverage; retain AVAILABLE/YES only for the scope actually analyzed successfully.
+- `lsp-evidence:` names the tool, absolute workspace, target file/symbol and observed
+  result or log. When unavailable, describe discovery/setup attempts and their outcome.
+- `lsp-limitations:` states fallback coverage and remaining gaps. `NONE` is allowed
+  only with a reason after actual semantic use; it is never a default for an omitted LSP.
+
+Example when no integration is exposed:
+
+```text
+## Tooling
+- rust-lsp: UNAVAILABLE (no Rust LSP APIs exposed)
+- lsp-used: NO (no semantic calls executed)
+- lsp-evidence: Tool discovery found no rust-lsp APIs; setup not authorized.
+- lsp-limitations: Read definitions, callers and tests directly; inferred types and macro expansion were not verified by LSP.
+```
+
+Absence of LSP is not itself a code defect and does not automatically require
+ESCALATE. Continue with exact-source inspection and existing compiler/test evidence.
+If this resolves the review obligations, APPROVE remains possible with the limitation
+disclosed. If ordinary required analysis remains incomplete, use INCOMPLETE; unresolved
+memory/concurrency safety requires ESCALATE under the existing rules. Honor project
+policy if it explicitly requires LSP. LSP never replaces Cargo gates, Miri or Loom.
+
+The report validator checks declarations and consistency, not whether MCP calls really
+happened. Inspect the recorded tool evidence before trusting a claim of semantic use.

diff --git a/.agents/skills/rust-pr-review/scripts/clippy.sh b/.agents/skills/rust-pr-review/scripts/clippy.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f361d72
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.agents/skills/rust-pr-review/scripts/clippy.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Preserve Clippy's exit status independently of optional diagnostic presentation.
+set -uo pipefail
+export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never
+if [[ ${RUST_REVIEWDOG:-0} != 1 ]]; then
+  exec cargo clippy "$@"
+fi
+logs=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rust-review-clippy.XXXXXXXX") || exit 2
+printf 'Clippy/reviewdog evidence: %s\n' "$logs" >&2
+# Capture raw output without a pipeline; retain unfiltered compiler errors.
+cargo clippy --message-format=short --color=never "$@" > "$logs/clippy.log" 2>&1
+clippy_status=$?
+printf '%s\n' "$clippy_status" > "$logs/clippy.exit"
+cat "$logs/clippy.log" >&2
+reviewdog_bin=${RUST_REVIEWDOG_BIN:-reviewdog}
+if ! command -v "$reviewdog_bin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo 'reviewdog: NOT RUN (optional tool missing; Clippy result retained)' >&2
+  exit "$clippy_status"
+fi
+args=(-f=clippy -reporter=local -filter-mode=nofilter -fail-level=warning)
+if [[ -n ${RUST_REVIEWDOG_BASE:-} ]]; then
+  # Only a resolved commit hash enters reviewdog's shell diff command.
+  if base=$(git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options "${RUST_REVIEWDOG_BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null); then
+    args=(-f=clippy -reporter=local -filter-mode=added -fail-level=warning
+      "-diff=git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color $base --")
+  else
+    echo 'reviewdog: invalid base; displaying unfiltered diagnostics' >&2
+  fi
+fi
+"$reviewdog_bin" "${args[@]}" < "$logs/clippy.log" > "$logs/reviewdog.log" 2> "$logs/reviewdog.stderr"
+reviewdog_status=$?
+printf '%s\n' "$reviewdog_status" > "$logs/reviewdog.exit"
+cat "$logs/reviewdog.log" "$logs/reviewdog.stderr" >&2
+printf 'reviewdog: exit=%s (presentation only; Clippy exit=%s)\n' "$reviewdog_status" "$clippy_status" >&2
+if [[ ! -s "$logs/reviewdog.log" ]]; then
+  echo 'Empty reviewdog report is not evidence of Clippy PASS; inspect clippy.log.' >&2
+fi
+exit "$clippy_status"

 ## Project policy (configure)
 
+- Use the actual edition, MSRV, toolchain, lint levels and error conventions in this repo.
+- Review public API compatibility against the project's supported release baseline.
+- Check unsafe invariants, aliasing/lifetimes, ownership across FFI and Send/Sync claims.
+- Check async blocking, lock order, cancellation, bounded resource use and error paths.
+- Require tests for meaningful behavior changes where they protect against regressions.
+- Default checks: fmt, clippy, tests (including doctests), cargo-deny with deny.toml.
+- Default feature configuration: --all-features. Replace with the supported feature
+  matrix for mutually exclusive features; align local checks and CI.
+- Configure deny.toml using the project's license, advisory and source policy.
+- Only mark deny N/A if project policy explicitly makes it inapplicable; missing
+  cargo-deny or deny.toml means NOT RUN. If required evidence is absent, INCOMPLETE.
+- Spec PASS requires user requirements or PR acceptance criteria; commit claims alone
+  yield PARTIAL. No findings does not mean all requirements were verified.
+- For affected unsafe/FFI boundaries, targeted Miri tests and a separate aliasing/
+  provenance argument are required before approval. Use isolated exact-source probes
+  when existing tests do not cover the path and execution is authorized. Unknown FFI
+  guarantees, unavailable targeted execution or conflicting alias models require ESCALATE.
+  General tests passing under Miri are not a substitute. Follow the skill’s
+  references/MEMORY-VALIDATION.md and report the Memory safety section.
+- For affected async behavior, require targeted progress/deadlock, cancellation and
+  task-termination tests as applicable. For changed custom synchronization protocols,
+  require Loom models and an independent invariant/ordering argument. Missing relevant
+  evidence or incomplete models require ESCALATE. Follow references/CONCURRENCY-VALIDATION.md
+  and report the Concurrency section; green ordinary tests are not a substitute.
+- Semver-checks remain conditional; document applicability and skipped checks.
+
+The skill provides smell, safety and spec references under
+`.agents/skills/rust-pr-review/references/`. They inform judgment and do not override
+verified source, repository policy or explicit user instructions.
+
+## Project policy (configure)
+
 - Use the actual edition, MSRV, toolchain, lint levels and error conventions in this repo.
 - Review public API compatibility against the project's supported release baseline.
 - Check unsafe invariants, aliasing/lifetimes, ownership across FFI and Send/Sync claims.

+/// Decode a native-endian word; short inputs return None, unaligned input is allowed.
+pub fn read_word(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
+    let raw: [u8; 4] = bytes.get(..4)?.try_into().ok()?;
+    Some(u32::from_ne_bytes(raw))
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0ab2138
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/publication.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+#[cfg(feature = "model")]
+use loom::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
+#[cfg(not(feature = "model"))]
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
+
+/// One-shot publication. The owner calls publish exactly once.
+/// A reader observing Some must see the value passed to publish.
+pub struct Published {
+    value: AtomicUsize,
+    ready: AtomicBool,
+}
+impl Default for Published {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            value: AtomicUsize::new(0),
+            ready: AtomicBool::new(false),
+        }
+    }
+}
+impl Published {
+    pub fn publish(&self, value: usize) {
+        self.value.store(value, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        self.ready.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+    }
+    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Option<usize> {
+        self.ready
+            .load(Ordering::Acquire)
+            .then(|| self.value.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
+    }
+}
diff --git a/src/registration.rs b/src/registration.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..fd3ef0f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/registration.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+/// C-ABI registration retains a read-only buffer until unregister returns.
+pub struct Registration {
+    bytes: *mut [u8],
+    len: usize,
+    unregister: unsafe extern "C" fn(),
+}
+impl Registration {
+    /// Register a stable buffer with a foreign consumer.
+    ///
+    /// # Safety
+    /// Callbacks must form one valid registration pair. register may retain and read
+    /// the provided range but cannot write or free it. unregister must synchronously
+    /// stop all reads before returning and must not unwind. Calls must be serialized
+    /// by the owner; no other registration may replace the active one.
+    pub unsafe fn new(
+        bytes: Box<[u8]>,
+        register: unsafe extern "C" fn(*const u8, usize),
+        unregister: unsafe extern "C" fn(),
+    ) -> Self {
+        let len = bytes.len();
+        let bytes = Box::into_raw(bytes);
+        // SAFETY: allocation ownership stays with this raw-pointer owner. No Box
+        // or reference is recreated until all foreign reads have stopped.
+        unsafe { register(bytes.cast::<u8>(), len) };
+        Self {
+            bytes,
+            len,
+            unregister,
+        }
+    }
+    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
+        self.len
+    }
+    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
+        self.len == 0
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Registration {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        // SAFETY: constructor contract guarantees synchronous quiescence.
+        unsafe { (self.unregister)() };
+        // SAFETY: this owns the original Box allocation; unregister stopped all
+        // reads and no other owner frees it. Reconstruct exactly once.
+        unsafe { drop(Box::from_raw(self.bytes)) };
+    }
+}
diff --git a/src/service.rs b/src/service.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0dd3a8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/service.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+use std::collections::VecDeque;
+use tokio::sync::{Mutex, oneshot};
+use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
+
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub struct Service {
+    count: Mutex<u64>,
+}
+impl Service {
+    pub async fn snapshot(&self) -> u64 {
+        *self.count.lock().await
+    }
+    pub async fn increment_and_snapshot(&self) -> u64 {
+        {
+            let mut count = self.count.lock().await;
+            *count += 1;
+        }
+        self.snapshot().await
+    }
+}
+
+/// Dequeue only when approval arrives. Dropping this future must preserve the queue.
+pub async fn approved_pop(
+    queue: &Mutex<VecDeque<u64>>,
+    approval: oneshot::Receiver<()>,
+) -> Option<u64> {
+    approval.await.ok()?;
+    queue.lock().await.pop_front()
+}
+
+/// Return only after the owned worker can no longer cause side effects.
+pub async fn stop_worker(worker: JoinHandle<()>) {
+    worker.abort();
+    let _ = worker.await;
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn snapshot_initial() {
+        assert_eq!(Service::default().snapshot().await, 0);
+    }
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn approved_delivery() {
+        let queue = Mutex::new(VecDeque::from([7]));
+        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
+        tx.send(()).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(approved_pop(&queue, rx).await, Some(7));
+    }
+}
diff --git a/tests/async_regressions.rs b/tests/async_regressions.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..64b4549
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/async_regressions.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+use runtime_bridge::service::{Service, approved_pop, stop_worker};
+use std::{
+    collections::VecDeque,
+    future::Future,
+    task::{Context, Poll, Waker},
+    time::Duration,
+};
+use tokio::sync::{Mutex, oneshot};
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn nested_lock_completes() {
+    let service = Service::default();
+    let value =
+        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(100), service.increment_and_snapshot()).await;
+    assert_eq!(value.expect("nested lock did not complete"), 1);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn cancel_before_approval_preserves_item() {
+    let queue = Mutex::new(VecDeque::from([7]));
+    let (_approval, rx) = oneshot::channel();
+    let mut operation = Box::pin(approved_pop(&queue, rx));
+    let mut cx = Context::from_waker(Waker::noop());
+    assert!(matches!(operation.as_mut().poll(&mut cx), Poll::Pending));
+    drop(operation);
+    assert_eq!(queue.lock().await.front(), Some(&7));
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn stopped_worker_cannot_receive_more_work() {
+    let (started_tx, started_rx) = oneshot::channel();
+    let (release_tx, release_rx) = oneshot::channel();
+    let (effect_tx, effect_rx) = oneshot::channel();
+    let worker = tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let _ = started_tx.send(());
+        if release_rx.await.is_ok() {
+            let _ = effect_tx.send(());
+        }
+    });
+    started_rx.await.unwrap();
+    stop_worker(worker).await;
+    let received_more_work = release_tx.send(()).is_ok();
+    if received_more_work {
+        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(100), effect_rx)
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .unwrap();
+    }
+    assert!(
+        !received_more_work,
+        "side effect observed after stop returned"
+    );
+}
diff --git a/tests/memory.rs b/tests/memory.rs

+++ b/tests/memory.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+use runtime_bridge::{bytes::read_word, registration::Registration};
+use std::cell::Cell;
+
+#[test]
+fn short_slice_rejected() {
+    assert_eq!(read_word(&[1]), None);
+}
+
+thread_local! { static RETAINED: Cell<*const u8> = const { Cell::new(std::ptr::null()) }; }
+unsafe extern "C" fn retain(ptr: *const u8, _: usize) {
+    RETAINED.with(|p| p.set(ptr));
+}
+unsafe extern "C" fn release() {
+    RETAINED.with(|p| p.set(std::ptr::null()));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn ffi_storage_lives_until_unregister() {
+    // SAFETY: these callbacks are serialized on the test thread, retain read-only
+    // data, do not unwind, and release synchronously forgets the pointer.
+    let registration = unsafe { Registration::new(vec![42].into_boxed_slice(), retain, release) };
+    // SAFETY: the live registration is required to own the still-registered storage.
+    let value = RETAINED.with(|p| unsafe { p.get().read() });
+    assert_eq!(value, 42);
+    drop(registration);
+    assert!(RETAINED.with(|p| p.get().is_null()));
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8e11ce3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/publication.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+#[cfg(feature = "model")]
+#[test]
+fn publication_is_coherent() {
+    loom::model(|| {
+        let published = loom::sync::Arc::new(runtime_bridge::publication::Published::default());
+        let writer = published.clone();
+        let task = loom::thread::spawn(move || writer.publish(42));
+        if let Some(value) = published.snapshot() {
+            assert_eq!(value, 42);
+        }
+        task.join().unwrap();
+    });
+}
